title: The map on tensor presheaves in the second variable commutes with restrictions.
statement:
Let $C$ be a category with a Grothendieck topology $J$, and let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $(C,J)$. The category-object, category-morphism, ring and module universes are independent, denoted $u_C,v_C,r,m$. Retain the ambient hypotheses $J.\mathrm{HasSheafCompose}(\mathrm{forget}_2\,\mathrm{CommRingCat}\,\mathrm{RingCat})$, $J.\mathrm{WEqualsLocallyBijective}(\mathrm{AddCommGrpCat}^{m})$, and $\mathrm{HasWeakSheafify}(J,\mathrm{AddCommGrpCat}^{m})$ of the attached Lean declaration. Let $M,N,N'$ be presheaves of modules over the underlying ring presheaf of $A$, and let $g:N\to N'$ be a morphism of module presheaves [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For $Q=N,N'$ write $T_Q=M\otimes_{p,A}Q$ for the sectionwise tensor presheaf [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product], so $T_Q(U)=M(U)\otimes_{A(U)}Q(U)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For each $U\in C^{\mathrm{op}}$, let $h_U=\mathrm{id}_{M(U)}\otimes g_U:T_N(U)\to T_{N'}(U)$ be the $A(U)$-linear map determined by $h_U(x\otimes y)=x\otimes g_U(y)$. For every $f:U\to V$ in $C^{\mathrm{op}}$, put $\rho=A(f):A(U)\to A(V)$. Then
$$\mathrm{Res}_{\rho}(h_V)\circ T_N(f)=T_{N'}(f)\circ h_U$$
as $A(U)$-linear maps from $T_N(U)$ to $\mathrm{Res}_{\rho}T_{N'}(V)$, where $\mathrm{Res}_{\rho}$ means restriction of scalars: the underlying abelian group and map are unchanged and $a\in A(U)$ acts through $\rho(a)$. Thus the sectionwise maps $\mathrm{id}\otimes g$ commute with restrictions.

proof.text: Fix $f:U\to V$ and put $\rho=A(f)$. By the tensor universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the $A(U)$-bilinear pairing $(x,y)\mapsto x\otimes g_U(y)$ defines $h_U$, and similarly for $h_V$. By [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product], $T_Q(f)$ sends $x\otimes y$ to $M(f)(x)\otimes Q(f)(y)$. It is $A(U)$-linear into the target with scalar action restricted along $\rho$: the two factor restrictions are $\rho$-semilinear by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. In particular the balanced relation is preserved, since the images of $(ax)\otimes y$ and $x\otimes(ay)$ are both $\rho(a)(M(f)(x)\otimes Q(f)(y))$. Restriction of scalars changes no underlying function, so both composites in the statement have the indicated common source and target.

proof.text: For $x\in M(U)$ and $y\in N(U)$ the first composite has value $M(f)(x)\otimes g_V(N(f)(y))$, while the second has value $M(f)(x)\otimes N'(f)(g_U(y))$. These formulas follow directly from the tensor pairings of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the restriction formula of [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product]. The two second factors are equal because $g$ is a morphism of presheaves: $g_V\circ N(f)=N'(f)\circ g_U$, by the definition of morphisms in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Hence the two composites agree on every pure tensor.

proof.text: The source $M(U)\otimes_{A(U)}N(U)$ is generated as an $A(U)$-module by pure tensors, by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Both composites are $A(U)$-linear into the same restricted module. Their agreement on the generators therefore implies agreement on every finite linear combination, hence equality as module morphisms. Since $f$ was arbitrary, this proves the required naturality equation.

theorem siteTensorSecondMap_naturality
    (M : PresheafOfModules.{m} (A.obj ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat))
    {N N' : PresheafOfModules.{m} (A.obj ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)} (g : N ⟶ N')
    {U V : Cᵒᵖ} (f : U ⟶ V) :
    (siteTensorPresheaf M N).map f ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (A.obj.map f).hom).map
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : M.obj V →ₗ[A.obj.obj V] M.obj V)
            (g.app V).hom)) =
      ModuleCat.ofHom (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : M.obj U →ₗ[A.obj.obj U] M.obj U)
        (g.app U).hom) ≫ (siteTensorPresheaf M N').map f := by
